ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence screening against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) consolidated list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Korean government's own sanctions list. Screening must include Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) from domestic and foreign jurisdictions, with enhanced scrutiny for high-risk countries. The screening process must be documented, and any positive hits must be escalated to the compliance officer for risk assessment and potential filing of a suspicious transaction report (STR) with KOFIU. Continuous monitoring is required throughout the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Company Registration System (i-REG)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul). Romanized names are allowed as secondary names but must be transliterated phonetically. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a business type descriptor, (3) a liability form indicator, and (4) a legal form suffix (e.g., 'Yuhan Hoesa' for LLC).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court Registry within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name is not confusingly similar to existing names and why it complies with the naming conventions. The registry will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. The applicant may also submit a revised name application at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for the shipbuilding industry due to strict tax and banking requirements. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for VAT registration and corporate tax purposes. Banks also require a physical address for opening corporate accounts. Therefore, a physical office in Korea is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered office is actually occupied by the company; (2) Ensure that the company name is displayed at the entrance; (3) Keep business records and accounting books at the office; (4) Have a designated representative to receive official correspondence. Risk: Moderate. The National Tax Service and the registry may conduct unannounced inspections, especially for newly formed companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting Articles of Incorporation and Power of Attorney
Notarization and apostille fees for foreign documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part III (Companies) Chapters governing Yuhan Hoesa and general incorporation registration; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended), Articles 6 and 8; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 8566, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Supreme Court Rules on Registration of Companies; Local Tax Act (registration license tax and education surtax).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Registry Office, Seoul Central District Court, with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; e-filing through the Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration System at www.i-eregi.go.kr; foreign investment reporting acceptance through KOTRA/Invest Korea in consultation with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified and notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa together with the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa filed under the Supreme Court Registration Rules; the incorporation becomes effective upon entry in the Commercial Register and issuance of the Certified Registration Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act; the subscribers may fix capital at any amount, including KRW 1. However, for a commercial shipyard operating as ISIC 3011 and to satisfy the facility and financial-capacity examination of the Shipbuilding Industry Promotion Act and prudent foreign lenders, the Company should initially contribute at least KRW 300,000,000 (approximately USD 225,000). Foreign capital brought into Korea must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may be held temporarily in a foreign-capital deposit account at a licensed foreign-exchange bank; once the company is registered, such funds must be transferred to the Company's corporate operating account and converted to Korean won as required. No government-administered blocked account is required for the Yuhan Hoesa itself, but bank escrow accounts should be established for ship-purchase maritime installment LCs and project-secured escrow payments.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR YUHANGHOESA CO., LTD. (A YUHAN HOESA): RESOLVED, THAT after due consideration of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the Company's proposed corporate objects, the draft Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting are adopted in final form and shall be executed and submitted for notarization and registration. RESOLVED, THAT the business object of the Company includes the commercial shipbuilding, construction, repair, conversion, outfitting, and delivery of deep-sea dry cargo vessels and ocean container vessels, including hull block fabrication, steel cutting and assembly, marine equipment procurement, painting, testing, sea trials, ship repair and the operation, lease, and maintenance of a shipyard, all as classified under ISIC 3011 and NAICS 336611. RESOLVED, THAT the initial membership capital of the Company is set at KRW 300,000,000 divided into 300,000 contribution units of KRW 1,000 each; the subscription table is approved; every founding member shall pay the full subscription amount to a bank account in the Company's name before the registration of incorporation; the directors and the Company secretary are authorized to obtain capital deposit certificates and to record contribution units in the members' register. RESOLVED, THAT the registered office of the Company shall be located at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, namely the principal office address in the Republic of Korea, and the operating shipyard shall be the physical yard address shown in the facility schedule; the Representative Director is authorized to execute or accept the lease, title, or right-of-use documents and to submit the registered-office adoption statement to the registry. RESOLVED, THAT the Company shall open and maintain corporate operating accounts, foreign-currency accounts, letter-of-credit facilities, and escrow accounts at any licensed commercial or foreign-exchange bank in Korea, and the management team is authorized to negotiate, sign, and operate maritime installment letters of credit, performance guarantees, refund guarantees, and escrowed progress-payment facilities for container-vessel construction contracts. RESOLVED, THAT the following statutory officers are appointed for the first term: the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, one or more Directors, a statutory Auditor, and a shipyard licensee manager; each officer accepts office and shall execute the prescribed consent forms and deposit their registered seals with the registry. RESOLVED, THAT the Representative Director, the Company secretary, and the foreign-investment counsel are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, sign, file, pay, and prosecute all incorporation applications, business registrations, Shipbuilding Business Registration with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, environmental impact assessments, fire safety permits, civil defense clearing, industrial workplace safety approval, and all related documents required to commence lawful construction and operation of the shipyard. RESOLVED, THAT any one of the authorized officers may take any ancillary action necessary to make these resolutions effective, including the issuance of certificates, opening of accounts, and appointment of local agents, and all prior actions taken in furtherance of the formation are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation, Foreign Investment Notification, and Opening of Foreign Capital Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA/Invest Korea Foreign Investment Support Center at www.investkorea.org, with the local foreign-exchange bank authorized under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability check for the Korean entity name and reserve the corporate trade name through the certified attorney's court-registry name search. If any shareholder or member is a non-resident foreign investor, file the Foreign Investment Report under Article 6 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank before remitting the contribution. The report must state the total foreign investment amount, the number of contribution units subscribed, the proposed Yuhan Hoesa object, and the shipyard business plan. After the report acceptance certificate is issued, open a temporary foreign-capital deposit account or escrow-style investment account at a licensed foreign-exchange bank and receive the remittance. Secure a bank certificate of receipt of funds.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate certificate of the foreign investor with apostille or consular legalization
Power of attorney appointing the Korean attorney-in-fact or formation agent
Draft Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language with the corporate name and ISIC 3011 business object
Articles of incorporation and board resolution of the foreign parent investor
Source-of-funds statement and bank reference for AML/KYC clearance
Foreign investment report form, foreign exchange bank remittance instructions, and account-opening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank issues a query, file a supplementary statement or corrected foreign investment report within 5 business days. If the report is rejected because the object, amount, or contribution-unit description is inconsistent, amend the Articles of Incorporation and re-file before executing any further remittance; administrative review may be requested through the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the district of the proposed registered office, together with the licensed commercial or foreign-exchange bank receiving the capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation conforming to the Yuhan Hoesa provisions of the Commercial Act. All founding members or their duly authorized attorneys must appear before a Korean notary public to execute the instrument. The articles must state the trade name, the shipbuilding objects, the registered office, the amount of capital, the contribution units, the value and type of each contribution, the names and addresses of members, and the number of directors and auditor. Upon notarization, pay the full subscription amount into a bank account opened in the name of the Company, or transfer the foreign capital from the temporary account into the Company's operating account. Obtain an unencumbered balance confirmation or capital deposit certificate from the bank.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including ISIC 3011 commercial shipbuilding object
Foreign Investment Report acceptance certificate from KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank
Executed power of attorney with notarization and apostille or consular legalization
Identification documents and KYC forms for all founding members, directors, and auditor
Bank certificate showing receipt of the full paid-in capital in the Company's account
Written consent of each statutory officer to accept office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify because the corporate object or contribution structure is ambiguous, revise the Articles of Incorporation, resubmit for notarization, and obtain fresh consents. If the capital deposit certificate shows a shortfall, cure the deficiency by remitting the balance and obtain a corrected certificate before the registration step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Civil Registry Office, Seoul Central District Court, or the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; e-filing via www.i-eregi.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after capital payment and notarial execution, file the application for registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank deposit certificates, consent forms of directors and auditor, foreign investment acceptance certificate, and proof of payment of the local registration license tax and education surtax. The court registration section will examine the existence and legality of the statutory officers, the registered office, the total capital, and the adequacy of the corporate object. Upon approval, the court enters the Company in the commercial register and issues the Certified Registration Matters and the corporate seal registration receipt. The date of registration is the date of incorporation of the legal entity.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa under the Supreme Court Registration Rules
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate or paid-in capital verification
Acceptance forms and identification of directors and auditor
Foreign Investment Report certificate if the investor is foreign
Power of attorney and legalized corporate documents of the foreign investor
Receipt showing payment of registration license tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for correction, respond electronically or in person within 5 business days with the missing document or corrected registration form. If the application is rejected, amend the defective item and re-file under the same application number; a petition may be made to the registry division, and subsequently administrative litigation in the District Court is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Corporate Seal Registration, and Activation of Operational, LC, and Escrow Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Tax Service office through Hometax at www.hometax.go.kr; Commercial Registration Division for seal registration; licensed foreign-exchange bank for payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the issuance of the Certified Registration Matters, register the corporate seal of the representative director with the court registry and obtain an original seal certificate. File the Business Registration Application with the National Tax Service within one month of incorporation to obtain the Business Registration Certificate and corporate taxpayer identification number. Use the business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and registered office lease contract to activate the Company's operating bank accounts. Establish separate foreign-currency and escrow accounts for maritime installment letters of credit, performance guarantees, and refund guarantees. Complete post-investment foreign investment reporting through KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank and obtain the Foreign Investment Certificate to secure dividend and capital repatriation rights.
required_dossiers: Certified Registration Matters of the Company
Corporate seal registration certificate
Business Registration Application and registered office lease or ownership certificate
Articles of Incorporation, tax identification number, and officer identification
Bank account opening forms, beneficial ownership declaration, and KYC documents
Foreign Investment Certificate if the entity has foreign investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the business registration because of an address mismatch, file an amended lease and a revised registered-office excerpt. If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence for the maritime LC facility, provide a shipbuilding business plan, source-of-wealth statements, and current owner or lease documentation for the shipyard assets.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Shipbuilding Business Registration and Shipyard Industrial License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shipbuilding Industry Promotion Division, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, with technical pre-screening by Korea Offshore & Shipbuilding Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as a shipbuilder under Article 6 of the Shipbuilding Industry Promotion Act and Article 7 of its Enforcement Decree before commencing production. Prepare an application for Shipbuilding Business Registration accompanied by proof of ownership or long-term lease of the shipyard and waterfront facilities, a detailed facility list showing dry dock, slipway, quay, block assembly shop, cutting and welding equipment, gantry cranes, and paint booths, evidence of technical personnel, and a certified organization chart. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy will review the sufficiency of facilities, financial capacity, and technical competence. Upon approval, the authority issues the Shipbuilding Business Registration Certificate. The certificate must be maintained as a condition of maritime export-credit facilities, and every vessel construction installment LC and escrow agreement should reference this certificate.
required_dossiers: Shipbuilding Business Registration application on the MOTIE prescribed form
Shipyard ownership or long-term lease contracts and rights to use the dry dock and quay
Facility list, major equipment schedule, and production capability statement
Technical staff roster with licenses and qualifications
Certified Registration Matters, Business Registration Certificate, and Articles of Incorporation
Environmental impact assessment decision or environmental operating permits for the shipyard
Civil defense and fire safety inspection reports for the yard
Paid-in capital certificate, financial statements, or bank facility evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOTIE rejects or conditions the registration because of insufficient dock capacity or financial capacity, provide additional undertaking documents, lease additional berth capacity, or increase paid-in capital and file a revised application. A request for reconsideration may be submitted within 30 days, followed by an appeal to the Administrative Appeals Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment Compliance, Civil Defense Fire Permit, and Occupational Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Impact Assessment Division, Ministry of Environment, with Korea Environment Corporation as review agency; local fire department under the National Fire Agency; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For construction, expansion, reclamation, or dredging of the shipyard, complete a full Environmental Impact Assessment or a prior environmental review before any physical development of the yard. Submit the environmental impact assessment report to the Ministry of Environment through the Korea Environment Corporation, conduct the required public consultations, obtain the consent or consultation from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for coastal and seawaters, and secure the final EIA approval from the permitting authority. After the EIA decision, obtain wastewater discharge and air emission permits under the Water Environment Conservation Act and the Clean Air Conservation Act, register as a waste generator in the Allbaro e-manifest system, obtain the building and fire-fighting installation completion inspection, receive the civil defense evacuation and shelter plan approval for the worksite, and arrange a structural safety inspection of the dry dock and gantry cranes. KOSHA must approve the occupational safety and health management plan for the shipyard before production starts.
required_dossiers: EIA report and supplementary environmental surveys for coastal water, marine sediment, air quality, noise, and waste
MOE and Korea Environment Corporation consultation decisions
Water pollutant discharge permit and air emission permits
Allbaro hazardous waste manifest registration and disposal contracts
Fire safety completion inspection certificate and civil defense shelter plan
Structural safety report for dry dock, quays, cranes, and heavy-load transfer systems
Occupational safety and health management plan approved by KOSHA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Environment requests supplemental studies, commission the additional field tests and respond within the prescribed period. If the fire department defers the fire permit, implement the corrective fire safety measures and re-inspect. Any adverse permit decision may be appealed through the administrative appeals process and ultimately to the Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Shipbuilding Industry Promotion Division, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, with technical pre-screening by Korea Offshore & Shipbuilding Association and interface with the Korea Environment Corporation, National Fire Agency, and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipbuilding Business Registration Certificate issued under Article 6 of the Shipbuilding Industry Promotion Act and Article 7 of its Enforcement Decree, authorizing the construction, repair, conversion, and delivery of ocean-going commercial vessels including container ships.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Impact Assessment Division, Ministry of Environment, with review and project management support from Korea Environment Corporation and consultation with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for coastal waters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act because a commercial shipyard with dry dock, slipway, quay, block assembly workshops, reclamation works, or waterfront dredging normally exceeds the statutory project site and development thresholds. If the project remains below the full EIA threshold and involves only minimal physical development, a Prior Environmental Review and environmental assessment report will apply; the environmental classification must be confirmed in writing by the Ministry of Environment before issuance of construction permits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from painting, blasting, degreasing, electroplating, washing, and dock flushing must meet effluent limitations typical of the Water Environment Conservation Act, including COD at or below 40 mg/L, BOD at or below 30 mg/L, suspended solids at or below 30 mg/L, oil and grease at or below 5 mg/L, total nitrogen at or below 60 mg/L, total phosphorus at or below 8 mg/L, lead at or below 0.1 mg/L, and hexavalent chromium at or below 0.05 mg/L, with stricter standards in any total pollution load control zone. Air emissions from paint and coating operations must comply with volatile organic compound stack concentration limits of not more than 40 ppm as toluene equivalent and capture and control efficiency above 95 percent; asbestos or lead abatement from vessel retrofits must follow the Clean Air Conservation Act and occupational exposure limits. Hazardous wastes from blasting grit, spent paint, solvents, waste oils, and marine antifouling compounds must be stored safely, manifested through the Allbaro e-manifest system, and transferred to a licensed waste treatment operator within the permitted storage period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil defense and fire safety approvals must include the Fire-Fighting System Installation and Maintenance Safety Certificate, fire completion inspection certificate, evacuation route and assembly area approval, hazardous material storage authorization, and compliance with the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Management of Fire-Fighting Systems. The structural integrity of dry docks, slipways, floating docks, and gantry cranes must be certified by a licensed structural engineer and reviewed by the Korea Infrastructure Safety Corporation. The shipyard must obtain the workplace safety and health clearance from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency covering occupational exposure to welding fumes, noise, painting solvents, confined space entry, crane lifting operations, and

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Export declarations are made through Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the UNI-PASS electronic system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity: (1) determine whether a domestic business place exists in Korea; if none, appoint a statutory tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes. (2) Prepare certified copies of the foreign entity's registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of identity of the responsible officer, and a power of attorney naming the Korean tax representative. (3) Submit the application for business registration to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the tax representative or domestic business place, or via the HomeTax portal, including the VAT registration disclosure required for non-resident enterprises. (4) The NTS will issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the Korean Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax and VAT purposes. (5) If the foreign entity supplies goods or services in Korea without a fixed place of business, use the tax representative for all HomeTax filing, e-tax invoice issuance, and refund claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean tax system does not provide a check-the-box or free-form entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is per se a domestic corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the Corporate Tax Act; no hybrid mismatch entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. All persons supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register as VAT entrepreneurs regardless of turnover. A special small-business simplified taxpayer regime applies to annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000 solely for VAT calculation and filing purposes, not as a registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice issuance is mandatory for VAT entrepreneurs; e-tax invoices must be issued to the customer and transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice service within the statutory deadlines. Retailers and service providers in prescribed consumer sectors must operate cash receipts through the NTS cash receipt system. There is no country-specific anti-fraud digital stamping regime such as SII or RAF; fiscal control is achieved through mandatory e-reporting and NTS real-time data linkage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero percent VAT applies under Korean VAT law to goods exported from Korea, including ocean container vessels and dry cargo deep-sea commercial ships delivered to foreign buyers, provided the export is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration, the goods are physically or constructively delivered outside Korea, and the export sale is settled in foreign currency. Qualifying offshore services and international shipping or shipbuilding support services performed abroad may also be zero-rated where prescribed by the VAT Act and Enforcement Decree.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (run through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS and confirming clearance of the vessel for export)
Bill of Lading or Vessel Delivery Certificate (evidencing export dispatch or constructive delivery of the vessel to the foreign consignee)
Commercial Invoice issued to the foreign buyer
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / Foreign Currency Receipt Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing full repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If required export documentation, foreign currency receipt, or genuine export status is missing, the zero-rated output VAT is clawed back, 10% VAT is assessed retroactively on the export supply, and interest and additional penalties are imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act. Intentional submission of false export declarations, forged bills of lading, or fraudulent foreign exchange settlement certificates is punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including criminal fines and imprisonment. Long-term maritime installment LC contracts should be supported by export proceeds collection schedules to avoid statutory penalty triggers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains free current-account convertibility for the KRW under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), but capital-account transactions are operated through a reporting and licensing regime, not through overt exchange restrictions. Current-account payments for trade, freight, insurance, and standard maritime services can be settled in KRW or foreign currency without prior approval if a licensed foreign exchange bank sees the supporting trade contract and customs declaration. Capital-account operations, including capital subscription by foreign shareholders in the shipbuilder, must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank; the Bank of Korea receives the record through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). No mandatory export-surrendering ratio applies to South Korean shipyards, but exported USD receipts must enter the banking system and can be held in domestic foreign-currency accounts before any KRW conversion at a licensed bank. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders requires audited financial statements proving distributable reserves, a corporate tax clearance certificate, and a disclosed FX purpose code; the bank will treat unresolved tax or undisclosed beneficial ownership as a withholding and AML obstacle. The net effect is high operational convertibility for genuine shipbuilding treasury flows, with non-resident, speculative, or anonymous access to KRW strictly curtailed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: six months from the date of export declaration under FETA Enforcement Decree; the exporter may use a licensed foreign exchange bank to extend the period when vessel milestones, classification certificates, or force majeure justify an extension. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%; no fixed percentage is surrendered to the central bank. However, proceeds must be received through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank and reported into the FEIS promptly; retention of export proceeds in an unlicensed overseas wallet or EMI account will be treated as a violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low for standalone treasury use. Korean FETA reserves foreign exchange business for banks licensed as foreign exchange banks. An offshore digital EMI not registered in Korea cannot receive and clear KRW, cannot become a correspondent to BOK-Wire+, and cannot lawfully hold mandatory custody of export proceeds for a domestic Korean LLC. Fintech products may be used only as a user interface over a licensed Korean sponsor bank, and even then the offshore EMI itself must not become a principal to the custody or settlement chain. A direct remittance into a non-Korean EMI before the Korean bank account would also undermine the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report and may be rejected by the Korean receiving bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch appearance is mandatory in practice for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced shipyard LLC. The statutory representative must attend the account-opening meeting with original corporate certificate, corporate seal confirmation, apostilled powers of attorney for any non-appearing directors, ARC or passport, and actual business evidence. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted because the Korean financial institution must directly verify identity and ask AML questions. Some banks permit video-based KYC only after the bank compliance committee approves an exception, but the initial account cannot be activated until a direct or delegated officer interview is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly formed overseas SPV is named buyer of one or more ocean container vessels, with stage payment obligations exceeding USD 20 million per milestone and no visible operating history or fleet ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified apostilled certificate of incorporation of the SPV; audited consolidated financial statements of the parent guarantor for the last three years; a company-relationship chart up to ultimate natural persons; bank reference letters from two unrelated banks; the full shipbuilding contract with delivery, refund, and default clauses; proof of economic substance for the SPV (registered office, operational staff, fleet or trade activity); and a UBO declaration aligned to 5% or greater ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade documents for imported steel plates, ship engines, and outfitting equipment show a cost variation of more than 5% from third-party market benchmarks or from previous same-supplier exports, placing the bank at risk of over- or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UNI-PASS import declarations and KCS duty receipts; commercial invoices and purchase orders with Incoterms and HS-8 digit descriptions; vendor bank account confirmation; third-party price indices or an independent marine surveyor cost quantification; ocean freight and marine insurance evidence; a variance memorandum with CFO and external auditor sign-off; and historical invoices for identical materials from the same manufacturer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Completed vessels may be flagged, chartered, or bareboat-registered in a jurisdiction associated with weak sanctions enforcement, or ship engines and navigation systems may contain dual-use components requiring Korean strategic item export authorization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user and end-use certificate for the vessel; contract provision prohibiting redelivery to sanctioned states or persons; Korean Strategic Items Notification assessment and, if applicable, export license; final vessel classification certificate from KR, ABS, DNV, or LR; confirmation that each equipment vendor completed OFAC, UN, EU, and Korean KFTC screening; and a post-delivery registry reporting covenant allowing the Korean bank to monitor the vessel registry change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder sends equity subscription through a third-party consulting company rather than the beneficial owner bank account, or the inward payment is fragmented below bank reporting thresholds to avoid FEIS filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FIPA prior report and KOTRA receipt; letter from each shareholder identifying the actual remittance account; source-of-wealth dossier including income tax returns, audited personal or corporate accounts, and asset valuation reports; board resolution approving share subscription and capital increase; notarized share register; bank certificate of paid-in capital; and an accounting firm capital verification certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign equity cash arriving into KR_YUHANGHOESA must be remitted to a licensed foreign exchange bank and to the segregated Capital Escrow Account or the Basic Operational Currency Account as designated in the FIPA report. The sender must issue SWIFT MT103 with the Korean shipyard legal entity name, corporate registration number, the exact purpose code for acquisition of equity in a domestic Korean company, and the beneficiary bank name. The Korean receiving bank completes the Foreign Exchange Information System filing, matches the remittance to the FIPA registration amount, confirms the identity of the foreign investor, and after final AML clearance issues the foreign-investment certificate used for capital verification. The shipyard auditor must prepare the paid-in capital verification, and the funds are released for shipbuilding procurement in KRW or foreign currency only after such verification. The remittance must never be structured into multiple sub-threshold wires, as Korean banks are mandated to report attempted structuring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Procurement of hull steel, engines, marine electronics, subcontract labor, and engineering services from foreign counterparties will be cleared through a licensed Korean bank using the following rails: direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for confirmed invoices under USD 5 million; standby and commercial import LCs (MT700 and MT710) for engine sets, steel slab and plate, and long-lead equipment; and documentary collections (documents against payment or acceptance) for standardized low-risk marine equipment. The bank will apply a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code on each disbursement, requiring match between invoice, UNI-PASS declaration, and freight receipt, and will not execute a payment to an offshore EMI or shell correspondent if sanctions screening of the beneficial owner fails. Export-side milestone receivables are settled by Maritime Installment LCs or Escrow Account drawings, and the Korean bank may deposit the proceeds into a USD escrow account until the customs export declaration is accepted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with licensed Korean foreign exchange banks, tenor aligned to contract milestone dates; no speculative net open position for the shipyard

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on KRW/USD permissible only when the Korean bank confirms an underlying shipbuilding revenue or cost exposure, the counterparty is a licensed FX bank or registered onshore bank, and the notional is reported to FEIS above threshold

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to stabilize long-term USD financing into KRW cash flows for working capital and construction finance, capped at the outstanding project debt and requiring bank credit approval

Vanilla KRW/USD options for protection against adverse currency moves are permissible when embedded in a zero-premium risk-reversal or capped forward program approved by bank compliance; exotic or leveraged products are not accepted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convene the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of members to approve the annual financial statements, appoint directors and statutory auditor (if required), and approve dividend distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Court of Registration (Registry Office) via the company registered agent - minutes must be filed with the local corporate registry if any director or officer change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM within the statutory window subjects the company to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; continuous non-compliance may lead to court-ordered special inspection, director suspension, and ultimately administrative strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (including the approved financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 fiscal year; automatic extension to April 30 if submitted through a certified tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalties of 20% of the assessed tax plus a daily overdue charge of 0.03% (annualized approximately 11%); persistent delinquency triggers bank and asset seizure and the company may be forcibly deregistered as a defunct corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local income tax surtax return on the corporate income tax assessed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local autonomous government (City/County/District) through the integrated national-local tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 of the following calendar year for a December 31 fiscal year (30 days after the corporate tax deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency charge of 10% of the unpaid surtax, plus 0.03% daily interest; prolonged non-payment permits the local government to seize property and cancel the business operation license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor independent audit report and audited financial statements filed with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one week after the Annual General Meeting (AGM), and no later than 3 months and one week after the fiscal year-end (by April 7 for a December 31 fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the external audit report subjects the company to fines up to KRW 50 million (approx. USD 38,000) under the Act on External Audit; the FSS may publicize the violation and refer the matter to financial regulators, potentially resulting in revocation of corporate benefits and further administrative proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report on the status of foreign direct investment, including changes in foreign ownership and management, submitted to the authorities to maintain foreign-invested enterprise status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the end of the month following the fiscal year-end (i.e., January 31 for a December 31 fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file renders the company ineligible for foreign-invested enterprise tax incentives and may result in a fine of up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,800); repeated non-compliance can lead to cancellation of foreign investment registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, as applied to a Yuhan Hoesa, mandatory independent CPA audit applies if, as of the end of the preceding financial year, any of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (i) total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9,200,000); (ii) annual net sales exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 (approx. USD 7,700,000); (iii) the average number of full-time employees exceeds 300; or (iv) total liabilities exceed KRW 5,000,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800,000). A commercial shipyard of the target scope is highly likely to surpass these thresholds, thus a statutory audit is compulsory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), as adopted by the Republic of Korea, are the definitive framework for all statutory audit target companies. For companies not meeting the audit threshold, the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for SMEs may be used; however, a globally operating shipyard dealing with maritime installment letters of credit and escrow accounts is obliged to follow K-IFRS for accurate cross-border revenue recognition.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose an annual confirmation filing solely for ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) purposes. However, any change in the LLC members' equity ownership (transfer, issuance, or succession) must be reported to the corporate registry within two weeks of the change. Additionally, under the AML and financial information laws, the company must maintain an accurate shareholder and beneficial ownership register and notify the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) of any beneficial owner change within 30 days from the date of the transaction.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 1,500 per year for a standard registered office and agent service, inclusive of government mail forwarding and statutory filing alerts
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 20,000 to USD 80,000 per year for a mid-to-large commercial shipyard with multi-currency transactions, inventory valuation, and long-term construction contracts

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone (Songdo, Busan-Jinhae, etc.) may grant 50% to 100% corporate income tax exemption for up to 10 years; R&D super-deductions of 30% to 50% apply to qualifying shipyard design and engineering expenditures; job creation and facility investment tax credits are available; Korea does not operate a separate patent box, but a proportion of qualifying patent and IP-derived income may be credited under R&D incentive schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 91 (Corporate Income Tax Return and Calculation Statement) filed through the HomeTax electronic filing portal of the National Tax Service; non-resident corporate filers use the Non-Resident Corporate Income Tax Return module on the same portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; semi-annual preliminary returns are required for the first six months (due within two months after the half-year end) and the annual return covers the full fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return is due within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end the deadline is March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension is available if a certified tax accountant prepared the return, and a further extension can be allowed when foreign subsidiaries are consolidated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and legal reference data: registered name of the Yuhan Hoesa, business registration number, head office address, representative director, accounting period, business classification code (ISIC 3011 for shipbuilding), and resident/non-resident status of the company and its owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean resident shipyard must identify all non-resident shareholders with their foreign entity registration numbers. If the filing is made for a non-resident Yuhan Hoesa with no Korean permanent establishment, the simplified non-resident form should be used and the return must not offset expenses incurred outside Korea against Korean-source income. The tax representative’s power of attorney must be attached to all filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement data: total gross revenue from ocean-going container vessel construction, ship sales and after-sales services, cost of sales, gross profit, SG&A expenses, operating income, non-operating income/expenses, and net income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue from maritime installment letters of credit and escrow-based construction contracts only under the percentage-of-completion method if all Korean revenue recognition requirements are met; otherwise use the completed-contract method at completion. All intercompany transactions, including hull procurement from the parent and technical services from the IP licensor, must be supported by written agreements, internal functional analyses, and contemporaneous economic substantiation before any deduction is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: financial net income plus disallowed expenses and non-deductible reserves minus tax-exempt income and statutory special deductions, yielding adjusted taxable base before any loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back cross-border management fees, royalty payments, and interest charged to the shipyard unless the payer can establish the actual provision of services, arm's-length pricing, and beneficial recipient status. Loss carryforwards must be traced to previously approved tax returns; no carryforward is available against non-resident branch income attributable to a Korean permanent establishment if the parent is the treaty beneficiary and the branch profits are not subject to Korean tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and adjustments: foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, R&D and job-creation credits, free economic zone incentives, and any treaty-based modifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident Yuhan Hoesa can take a foreign tax credit only for withholding taxes imposed on Korean-source income by a foreign jurisdiction and only with the foreign TRC and tax voucher attached. Non-resident shareholders are not allowed to claim Korean R&D or investment credits directly; treaty-exempt or treaty-reduced income must be entered on the DTA claiming schedule, not as a credit line. Any claim for free economic zone exemption requires a certificate confirming the qualified business activity is substantially performed at the Korean shipyard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax base and rate schedule: progressive national corporate income tax rates applied to the computed taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The national statutory headline rate is 24% for taxable income over KRW 300 billion; lower brackets (10%, 20%, 22%) apply below that threshold, plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax for resident companies. Non-resident corporations without a Korean permanent establishment are not subject to the local surtax and are instead subject to final withholding tax on Korean-source dividends, interest, and royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability computation: tax payable after crediting preliminary payments, advance payments, employer withholding, and foreign tax credits; refund or balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border profit repatriation declared in the same fiscal year must be listed separately showing the statutory withholding rate, treaty-reduced rate, and explanations. The statutory outbound WHT is 22% for dividends, interest, and royalties unless a valid treaty claim is filed with a current TRC. If the final tax underpaid is at least 30% of the correct tax, an additional 20% neglect penalty is assessed; criminal referrals are triggered for fraudulent underpayments above KRW 50 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedules and cross-border disclosures: transfer pricing documentation (Master File, Local File, Country-by-Country Report), foreign financial accounts, non-loan financial transactions, and DTA relief forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Master File and Local File are mandatory when the aggregate amount of international related-party transactions exceeds KRW 10 billion in the fiscal year; a CbC report is required for groups with consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more. The schedule of foreign related-party transactions must disclose loans, intercompany services, IP royalties, and vessel sales. Any claim of over-capacity utilization or excessive deductions to a foreign affiliated shipbuilder without operating substance should be avoided; such transactions are subject to recharacterization and penalty tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a 20% general indifference penalty on unpaid tax (30% for negligent or fraudulent understatement), an additional 0.3% monthly surcharge for failure to pay, and a 10% penalty for omitted foreign transaction disclosures under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Willful non-filing or fraudulent filing over KRW 50 million is referred to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office as criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, exposing the representative director to imprisonment for up to ten years or a fine up to five times the evaded tax, plus designation as a serious tax evader with publication of the evasion data.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding + 2% local income tax surcharge) on outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless a lower tax treaty rate is substantiated
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief at the source, the Korean payer must obtain from the non-resident shareholder a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority, a completed DTA application statement, and a beneficial ownership declaration. The shareholder must demonstrate active business purpose, absence of conduit arrangements, and, for reduced dividend rates, maintenance of the required shareholding percentage for the minimum holding period (commonly at least 25% for 365 days). The Korean shipyard files the DTA claim together with the withholding return on the HomeTax portal, retains all substantiation, and applies the reduced rate from the first remittance. If the TRC or beneficial ownership certificates are incomplete, statutory WHT of 22% must be withheld. Where tax was over-withheld, an application for refund may be filed with the National Tax Service within five years, supported by the TRC and proof of legal and beneficial entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on cross-border interest and intellectual property royalties is 22% (20% national + 2% local surtax) in the absence of a treaty. Under Korea’s principal bilateral treaties, interest may be reduced to 5-15% and royalties to 10-15%, but only where the recipient is the beneficial owner and the OECD-compliant limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose test is satisfied. Back-to-back loans or IP chains with zero-function intermediaries are ignored for treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion for mandatory Master File and Local File on combined international related-party transactions; KRW 5 billion for the simplified Local File in certain defined service, interest, and IP categories; Country-by-Country Report threshold is consolidated group revenue of KRW 1 trillion
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not statute the Gulf-regime Economic Substance Regulations or the exact Core Income-Generating Activities label, but its substantive doctrines under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs and the Corporate Tax Act require that the shipyard conduct and direct the core business activities - vessel design, procurement, engineering, construction, supervision, and risk assumption - within Korea. A Yuhan Hoesa that merely books profit while its board and all key decision-making occur abroad will be disregarded, with income reattributed to the actual value-creating entity. Equivalent CIGA principles are applied in treaty claims to ensure the recipient is not a conduit, and shell entities without employees, premises, or business risk are denied DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenues from ocean-going container vessel construction or inflating deductible payments to a no-tax or low-tax interposed affiliate while the Korean shipyard executes all shipbuilding functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3(1) and Article 8 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, tax evasion by fraudulent or active concealment is punishable by imprisonment for up to ten years or a fine of up to five times the evaded tax; the National Tax Service also imposes a 20-30% penalty surcharge on the understated tax amount. Intentional underreporting above KRW 50 million is automatically referred to the prosecution service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may disregard the limited liability structure where the company is a sham or the director knowingly organizes a façade; the director becomes jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax and surcharges. The director may be added as a secondary taxpayer under the National Tax Collection Act, blacklisted as an illegal tax evader, subjected to a travel ban restricting departure from South Korea, and criminally sentenced to imprisonment for up to ten years with possible asset confiscation and restitution of the evaded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling newly built vessels to a related foreign distributor or IP-holding affiliate at a non-arm's-length price, or inserting a Hong Kong or Singapore shell with no employees or economic activity solely to access an advantageous treaty rate and accumulate profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 4 and 5 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs authorize the National Tax Service to reconstruct the transaction, impute taxable income to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, and impose a penalty of 20% (or 30% for reckless disregard) on the corrected tax base; the same facts may trigger denial of treaty benefits and foreign exchange controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who executes the intercompany agreements with knowledge of the sham is considered a de facto or shadow director under the Commercial Act, subject to civil damages for the company’s tax losses. If the company lacks assets to pay the additional tax, the director can be held personally liable under the National Tax Collection Act; repeated or serious manipulation leads to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment and an entry ban or travel blacklist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default and Fraudulent DTA Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, royalty payments, or intercompany interest to a non-resident shareholder without deducting the statutory 22% withholding, or submitting a forged, expired, or erroneously obtained Tax Residency Certificate to claim a treaty reduction for a non-beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Corporate Tax Act and the Local Income Tax Act assess the unpaid withholding tax, a 30% penalty for willful failure to withhold (50% in the case of fraudulent failure), and a 10% additional charge for false DTA claims. Improper use of a treaty to escape Korean tax is prosecuted as tax evasion, with fines and imprisonment available under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Withholding and remittance is an officer-level fiduciary duty; the representative director is personally liable for any withheld-not-remitted tax and penalties. A director who procures or participates in a fraudulent TRC claim may face asset restitution of the under-withheld amount, a travel ban (blacklisting) on grounds of outstanding tax delinquency, disqualification as a corporate director, and criminal imprisonment where severity warrants.
